analysis.title: Fed minutes: Almost all expected a further rate increase, a couple discussed a 50 bp move
key_insights: The October 27-28 FOMC minutes show most members supported holding rates steady, awaiting more information and, per a couple of members, to give businesses and households time to adjust to higher rates.
Holding rates was a close call for a few participants and some favoured a hike. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted to raise by 25 bp in October.

A few members who favoured a hike would have supported unchanged rates if it was 'clearly understood' that further tightening was likely. SEB reads this as possible criticism of Chair Warsh's communication policy, including his resistance to forward guidance. SEB expects Waller to be among the critics.
Almost all participants thought the Fed would likely have to raise rates further. A couple said a 50 bp hike in December could be appropriate if incoming inflation data were 'unfavorable'.

Most members expected inflation to return to target over time, citing waning tariff effects, a smaller energy contribution and easing price pressure from the AI buildout. The 'vast majority' saw upside risks to this outlook. SEB reads this as making a hike a precautionary step rather than a necessary one.

Much of the discussion centered on inflation risks from the AI buildout. The labour market was seen as stable and near maximum employment, with many seeing signs of modest tightening. A majority noted financial conditions had tightened since September.

SEB says the minutes are outdated because they predate stronger October payrolls and an upside CPI surprise in October that was relatively broad-based. Recent Fed comments have generally been hawkish, and Waller has been alone in discussing 50 bp steps.

SEB expects a 25 bp hike at the December 8-9 FOMC meeting and possibly another in March 2027. It sees risks skewed toward another increase, and expects the December projections to signal a large probability of at least one more hike in 2027.
Markets price a small probability of a larger December move (27 bp) and at least two more hikes by summer (81 bp by September).

tension_points.bull_case: SEB expects hikes in December and possibly March, as almost all participants saw further tightening ahead and recent data was strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Members are more split on the path after December, and most seem to prefer a gradual pace over a 50 bp move. Most members expect inflation to return to target.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A large surprise in the November employment report (4 December), financial conditions or Middle East developments before the December 8-9 meeting.
